news.title: Power and gas forwards rose on 16 October
news.summary: PEP-ICD’s 16 October close put Q1 2027 power at 17.58p/kWh and Summer 2027 at 12.72p/kWh; Summer 2027 rose £1.56/MWh that day. NBP day-ahead closed at 7.31p/kWh. These wholesale prices are not supplier offers.

news.title: Ofgem consults on activating Market Stabilisation Charge
news.summary: Ofgem proposed activating the dormant charge to mitigate supplier losses if wholesale prices fall sharply and customers switch. Responses are due by 29 October. It is a proposal, not an active charge.

news.title: Ofwat proposes £280,000 Hafren Dyfrdwy enforcement package
news.summary: Ofwat says the company breached wastewater and sewer obligations. The proposed package is funded by the company and shareholders, not customer bills, and remains subject to consultation until 6 November.

news.title: Thames Water reports support agreement with Class B creditors
news.source: Thames Water; London Stock Exchange announcement
news.summary: Thames Water said it had reached a transaction support agreement with certain Class B creditors, including holders of more than 60% of its Class B debt. Its recapitalisation proposal remains subject to ongoing discussions and approvals.

news.title: Winter gas eases while 2027 contracts rise
news.summary: Catalyst reported on 16 October that November 2026 gas had fallen to 213.65p/therm (7.29p/kWh) on 15 October as Norwegian supply recovered, while Summer 2027 and Winter 2027 contracts rose. Low European storage and LNG competition remained risks.

news.title: Nuclear industry argues for more baseload generation
news.summary: The Nuclear Industry Association said additional nuclear baseload could help address pressure on the UK power system. This is an industry position, not a new market price or government decision.

news.title: Thames Water asks customers to keep saving water amid drought pressures
news.summary: The company said dry conditions persisted in its catchment. It reported September rainfall at 50% of the long-term average and very little October rainfall by 6 October.

news.title: Ofgem chief sets out consumer-focused priorities
news.summary: Tim Jarvis highlighted consumer bills, flexibility and lowering electricity costs, and described the wholesale outlook ahead of winter as difficult.

news.title: MHHS programme publishes its latest weekly update
news.summary: The programme’s 14 October newsletter is its latest listed update. Check meter-data readiness, supplier implementation and how settlement or time-of-use changes are treated in contracts.

signal.label: Fix early
signal.title: Review winter renewals early as forward prices rose and the cap forecast remains elevated
signal.detail: The live APX 24-hour average is 14.98p/kWh. That is below the previous briefing’s 16.28p/kWh, but the rolling periods overlap and are not a like-for-like comparison. On 16 October, Q1 2027 power was 17.58p/kWh and Summer 2027 was 12.72p/kWh; Summer 2027 rose £1.56/MWh that day. NBP November gas was 7.40p/kWh on 16 October. PEP-ICD’s Summer 2027 gas close was 5.61p/kWh, while another source reported 5.51p/kWh for that date. The January 2027 household cap forecast is £1,999.28 a year against the current £1,723 cap. In the listed power curve, Summer 2028 is the cheapest delivery period at 8.07p/kWh and Q1 2027 is the most expensive at 17.58p/kWh. For gas, Summer 2028 is cheapest at 3.33p/kWh and Q1 2027 is most expensive at 7.43p/kWh. These are wholesale comparisons, not supplier quotes or a guarantee that fixing now will be cheaper.

invoice.intro: Business energy bills combine wholesale energy, networks, balancing, policy charges, tax and metering. Fixed contracts may bundle costs into unit and standing charges; pass-through contracts may show them separately. Rates below are carried forward where not refreshed for this intraday update. Check the cited publisher and your contract.

charges.name: Wholesale electricity
charges.whatItIs: The cost of electricity bought by the supplier on wholesale markets.
charges.onYourBill: Usually built into the unit rate; flexible contracts may show the purchasing basis separately.

charges.name: DUoS (distribution use of system)
charges.whatItIs: Regional charges for local distribution networks. Rates depend on location, voltage, time band and site capacity.
charges.onYourBill: May appear as time-band unit, fixed or capacity charges, or be bundled into the contract.

charges.name: TNUoS (transmission network use of system)
charges.period: 2026/27; previous briefing reported an average rise of about 60% from April 2026
charges.source: Energy Advice Hub; carried forward from previous briefing
charges.whatItIs: Charges for use of the national high-voltage transmission network. The previously reported average increase is not a site-specific rate.
charges.onYourBill: May be passed through as a daily or capacity charge, or included in the contract price.

charges.name: BSUoS (balancing services)
charges.whatItIs: NESO’s charge for balancing the electricity system, recovered through fixed six-month tariffs.
charges.onYourBill: May appear as a per-kWh pass-through charge or be bundled in the unit rate.

charges.name: Renewables Obligation (RO)
charges.whatItIs: Funds eligible renewable generation through supplier certificate obligations or buy-out payments.
charges.onYourBill: Usually passed through per kWh or included in the unit rate. Eligible EII certificate holders are exempt.

charges.name: Contracts for Difference (CfD) levy
charges.whatItIs: Funds payments that top up eligible low-carbon generators to their agreed strike prices.
charges.onYourBill: Usually a per-kWh pass-through line, subject to reconciliation. Eligible EII certificate holders are exempt.

charges.name: Nuclear RAB levy (Sizewell C)
charges.whatItIs: Quarterly levy funding Sizewell C under the Regulated Asset Base model.
charges.onYourBill: May appear as a per-kWh pass-through line. Check change-in-law terms on older fixed contracts. Eligible EII certificate holders are exempt.

charges.name: Capacity Market
charges.whatItIs: Pays capacity providers to be available when the system needs electricity. Supplier costs vary with demand and settlement arrangements.
charges.onYourBill: May be passed through per kWh, often with winter peak consumption affecting site charges.

charges.name: Feed-in Tariff (FiT) levy
charges.whatItIs: Supplier-recovered costs associated with the closed small-scale Feed-in Tariff scheme.
charges.onYourBill: May be bundled into the unit rate or shown as a pass-through charge. Eligible EII certificate holders are exempt.

charges.name: EII Support Levy
charges.whatItIs: Funds the network-charge compensation scheme for eligible energy-intensive industries. No single current customer £/MWh rate was verified.
charges.onYourBill: Suppliers may recover their levy costs through customer prices.

charges.name: EII exemption and network-charge compensation
charges.whatItIs: Eligible energy-intensive businesses may apply for exemptions from specified policy costs and compensation for specified network charges, subject to scheme rules.
charges.onYourBill: Give the current certificate to the supplier and check eligible consumption and charges are treated correctly.

charges.name: Climate Change Levy (CCL)
charges.whatItIs: A tax on taxable business energy supplies. Climate Change Agreement participants may qualify for reduced rates.
charges.onYourBill: Normally charged as a separate line before VAT; check site exemptions and any eligible reduced rate.

charges.name: VAT on electricity
charges.rate: 20% standard business rate; 0% for qualifying supplies during the temporary period
charges.period: Temporary 0% from 1 Oct 2026 to 31 Mar 2027 for qualifying supplies
charges.whatItIs: VAT treatment depends on the supply and site eligibility. The temporary zero rate does not apply to all business electricity.
charges.onYourBill: Check the VAT rate applied to each site and period of consumption.

charges.name: Metering and settlement charges
charges.whatItIs: May include meter operator, data collection, data aggregation and settlement services.
charges.onYourBill: May be a separate daily or monthly charge, or bundled into the standing charge.

charges.name: Wholesale gas
charges.whatItIs: The cost of gas bought by the supplier, commonly benchmarked to the NBP.
charges.onYourBill: Usually built into the p/kWh unit rate.

charges.name: Gas transportation (NTS and LDZ)
charges.period: Set by applicable tariffs and contract
charges.whatItIs: Charges for the national transmission system and local gas distribution networks, alongside applicable shipper and industry costs.
charges.onYourBill: May be bundled into unit and standing charges or shown separately on larger pass-through contracts.

charges.name: Green Gas Levy
charges.whatItIs: Funds the Green Gas Support Scheme through charges on licensed gas suppliers.
charges.onYourBill: Often recovered through the supplier’s standing or unit charge.

charges.name: Climate Change Levy (CCL)
charges.whatItIs: A tax on taxable business gas supplies. Climate Change Agreement participants may qualify for reduced rates.
charges.onYourBill: Normally charged as a separate line before VAT; check site exemptions and any eligible reduced rate.

charges.name: VAT on gas
charges.rate: 20% standard business rate; 5% on qualifying domestic-rate supplies
charges.whatItIs: VAT treatment depends on the supply and site eligibility. The temporary 0% electricity measure does not apply to gas.
charges.onYourBill: Check the VAT rate applied to the site and period of consumption.

charges.name: Gas metering charges
charges.whatItIs: Charges associated with the gas meter asset and meter services.
charges.onYourBill: May appear as a daily charge or be included in the standing charge.

updates.title: Temporary 0% VAT on qualifying electricity supplies
updates.detail: The temporary zero rate runs from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027 for qualifying supplies. It does not mean every business electricity supply is zero-rated; check site eligibility and invoice treatment.

updates.title: BSUoS fixed tariff 8 is in effect

updates.title: Q4 2026 nuclear RAB interim levy
updates.detail: The Sizewell C nuclear RAB interim levy is £3.754/MWh (0.3754p/kWh) for Q4 2026. Eligible EII certificate holders are exempt.

updates.title: CfD interim levy rates
updates.detail: The interim rate is £5.529/MWh (0.5529p/kWh) for October–December 2026 and £2.979/MWh (0.2979p/kWh) for January–March 2027. Eligible EII certificate holders are exempt.

updates.title: EII network-charge relief
updates.detail: Eligible energy-intensive industries receive 90% compensation on eligible network charges from the April 2026 claim month. No single customer £/MWh EII Support Levy rate was verified.

briefing.summary: Elexon’s live APX average for the 24 hours to 14:00 on Saturday 17 October was £149.83/MWh (14.98p/kWh), with a low of £87.77/MWh (8.78p/kWh) and a high of £214.70/MWh (21.47p/kWh). The average is £12.92/MWh below the previous briefing’s figure, but the rolling windows are not like-for-like. Wind was the largest listed generation source at 8,677 MW; grid carbon intensity was 47 gCO2/kWh. Latest verified power forwards, dated 16 October, rose: Q1 2027 was £175.82/MWh (17.58p/kWh) and Summer 2027 was £127.18/MWh (12.72p/kWh). PEP-ICD’s NBP day-ahead close was 214.29p/therm (7.31p/kWh) on 16 October, up from 210.53p/therm (7.18p/kWh) on 15 October. For Summer 2027 gas, sources report 161.52–164.53p/therm (5.51–5.61p/kWh) for 16 October; this briefing uses PEP-ICD’s 164.53p/therm. The current household cap is £1,723 a year for October–December. Cornwall Insight’s January forecast remains £1,999.28 a year, not an Ofgem decision.
